subject: science
passage: Saharan silver ants leave their nests at midday, when the surface of the desert sand can exceed 60°C and most other animals stay hidden. Their bodies are covered in tiny hairs with a triangular cross-section that reflect much of the sunlight striking them and help radiate excess heat. Even so, the ants must keep their trips short, racing across the sand in search of insects that have died in the heat. Their timing is no accident: the lizards that usually prey on ______ have by then retreated into the shade.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The animals the lizards prey on are the ants, a plural noun used throughout the passage. The pronoun is the object of the preposition "on," so it must be the plural object pronoun "them."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "It" is singular, but it must refer to the plural "ants"; the lizards do not prey on the sand or the shade.
explanation.B: Correct. "Them" is plural, matching "the ants," and is the object form needed after "on."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "They" is a subject pronoun; after the preposition "on," the object form "them" is needed.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Themselves" is reflexive and would refer back to the subject "the lizards," saying that lizards prey on lizards.
